title: SPADE: Sparse Pillar-based 3D Object Detection Accelerator for Autonomous Driving
problem: PointPillars-based 3D object detection methods overlook vector sparsity in pillar encoding, and existing sparse convolution accelerators only handle element-wise activation sparsity, missing the vector sparsity opportunities from pillar aggregation.
motivation: Efficient 3D object detection from point cloud data is critical for autonomous driving perception pipelines with stringent resource and latency requirements.
method: SPADE uses algorithm-hardware codesign—jointly designing the computation method and hardware together for efficiency. It has three parts: a dynamic vector pruning algorithm that identifies which groups of calculations can be skipped while maintaining detection accuracy, hardware that manages sparse data locations and transforms a standard 2D systolic array (a grid of parallel processing units) into a vector-sparse convolution accelerator, and a sparsity-aware dataflow optimization that schedules calculations through the hardware to maximize efficiency from skipped operations.
key_novelty: SPADE's core idea is algorithm-hardware codesign that targets vector sparsity (skipping entire groups of related calculations) in pillar-based encoding, whereas existing accelerators only exploit element-wise sparsity (skipping individual elements).
contributions: Dynamic vector pruning algorithm for pillar encoding sparsity
Sparse coordinate management hardware enabling vector-sparse convolution acceleration
Sparsity-aware dataflow optimization for hardware efficiency
Taped-out ASIC achieving 1.3-10.9× speedup and 1.5-12.6× energy savings versus dense accelerator

metrics.speedup: 1.3-10.9× vs dense accelerator, 4.1-28.8× vs server/edge platforms
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.5-12.6× vs dense accelerator, 90.2-372.3× vs server/edge platforms
